extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers and practitioners building or evaluating sarcasm-detection datasets and systems
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, filtering, evaluating, and releasing a large self-annotated sarcasm corpus (from Reddit) and specification of benchmark classification tasks for sarcasm detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major corpus evaluation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three major metrics of interest for evaluating our corpora: (1) size, (2) the proportion of sarcastic to non-sarcastic comments, and (3) the rate of false positives and false negatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also consider the quality of the text in the corpus and its applicability to other NLP tasks when comparing corpora.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corpus size (scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corpus should be large enough to support learning in both balanced and unbalanced label regimes (SARC: ~1.3M sarcastic comments; raw CSV contains ~533M comments overall).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A larger dataset enables both large-scale machine learning and deriving smaller benchmark tasks; report absolute counts of sarcastic and non-sarcastic examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class proportion / balancing
rubrics_metrics.description: Characterize and provide both unbalanced and balanced subsets: (unbalanced) reflect the natural low prevalence of sarcasm, (balanced) subsample to equalize labels for certain evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making balanced datasets, select one sarcastic and one non-sarcastic response per context (see similarity filtering guidance) and report prevalence statistics for each split.

rubrics_metrics.name: False positive / false negative measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate the rate of false positives (items labeled sarcastic incorrectly) and false negatives (sarcastic items unlabeled) induced by self-annotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use manual evaluation (authors used: random sample of 500 sarcastic and 500 non-sarcastic with full context). Example results reported: false positive rate 1.0%, false negative rate 2.0%. Document definitions used for FP and FN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-annotation validity filters (author-awareness and placement)
rubrics_metrics.description: To reduce noise from using the textual marker “/s” as the sarcasm label, restrict to comments whose authors have previously used “/s” (in the same month or earlier) and keep only comments where “/s” appears at the end of the comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This filter reduces false negatives from users unaware of the convention and false positives where “/s” is used in other senses; document the exact temporal criterion for 'previous use' (authors used same month or earlier).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subreddit and sense-disambiguation filtering
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude comments from subreddits where “/s” has alternate meanings (e.g., technical discussion of strike-through or web programming) to reduce sense-mismatch false positives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If alternate senses persist, consider restricting to well-moderated or topical subreddits that are unlikely to use “/s” in other senses (example: avoid programming subreddits; politics used as topic-specific subsample).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversation-structure filtering (exclude descendants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discard child comments (descendants) of sarcastic comments in a thread because annotation in such cases is extremely noisy (chains of sarcasm without explicit tags).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids ambiguous propagation of sarcasm labels through reply chains where subsequent comments may echo sarcasm without tagging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic preprocessing filters
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply standard preprocessing such as excluding comments that contain URLs, restricting characters to ASCII, and removing very short/long or non-sentence comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For evaluation subsamples the authors removed comments that are not complete sentences and kept only comments between 2 and 50 tokens long to produce cleaner evaluation data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manual evaluation protocol for corpus noise
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess corpus noisiness by manually checking random subsets of labeled and unlabeled comments with full conversation context to determine FP/FN rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors used 500 comments labeled sarcastic and 500 labeled non-sarcastic, providing local context to raters; define FP as '/s' present but not an annotation, FN as clearly sarcastic to human raters despite no tag. Note limitation: some sarcasm requires external knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release and data-format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide raw files sufficient for reproduction and flexible benchmark construction: (1) CSV array of comments (with author awareness flag and parent comment), (2) JSON hashtable of all comments/posts in conversation threads of sarcastic comments and siblings, (3) CSV array of sequences leading up to sarcastic comments with response labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document schema for each file, include identifiers linking back to original scraped dataset, and make code to reproduce benchmarks available (authors provided GitHub link).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary benchmark task specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Define a detection task: given a post and a sequence of comments, determine which comments among the responses to the last element in the sequence are sarcastic; datapoints consist of a conversation thread followed by responses and sarcasm labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure performance on this general task using average precision, recall and F1 scores. Provide full conversation thread and comment metadata to learning algorithms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced-label benchmark construction (pairwise choice)
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct a balanced task by selecting one sarcastic and one non-sarcastic response from each response set; the task becomes choosing which of two statements sharing context is sarcastic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To reduce near-duplicate selection of non-sarcastic statements, featurize statements using normalized sum of word embeddings and only choose non-sarcastic examples with similarity ≤ 0.95 to the sarcastic statement (authors used Common Crawl GloVe for this similarity). Measure performance by accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-specific subsampling and evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Create topic-restricted subsamples (e.g., politics subreddit) to test detection when background knowledge matters; ensure evaluators have sufficient topical background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors used a politics subsample (17K sequences, avg. sarcastic responses 23.2%) and observed different human agreement (higher Fleiss kappa). Report proportions and motivate topic selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature selection thresholds for bag-of-n-grams baselines
rubrics_metrics.description: When using bag-of-words or bag-of-bigrams, include only n-gram features that occur at least a minimum number of times in training (authors: ≥5 occurrences for 'all subreddits' experiments; ≥100 occurrences for the politics unbalanced task).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report which threshold was used per experiment and justify choice based on dataset size; authors noted that some simple metadata (length, scores) were not particularly informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation and baseline methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide simple baseline methods to establish benchmarks: Bag-of-Words, Bag-of-Bigrams, Sentence Embedding (elementwise sum of word embeddings), human baseline (multiple annotators, majority vote), and random baseline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify embedding model used for sentence embedding (authors: 1600-dimensional GloVe trained on Amazon product corpus), train-test split (authors: 80% train / 20% test), and how the random baseline selects sarcasm probability (set to average fraction of sarcastic responses in training set). Report accuracy/F1/precision/recall as appropriate; compare to human performance and report inter-annotator agreement (Fleiss kappa).

rubrics_metrics.name: Human evaluation protocol and agreement reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure human performance by presenting evaluators with tasks equivalent to algorithms (e.g., choose which of two statements is sarcastic), provide full context, use multiple annotators, and aggregate by majority vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors used 5 evaluators each given 100 samples; reported average and majority human performance as well as Fleiss kappa (0.5 on main dataset = moderate agreement; 0.67 on politics subsample = substantial agreement). Include details on sample sizes and how majority labels were formed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting classifier diagnostics and indicative features
rubrics_metrics.description: Report classifier diagnostics such as F1 or accuracy per task and list most positively/negatively weighted n-grams to indicate what signals classifiers rely on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors displayed lists of top positive/negative n-grams with weights from the Bag-of-Bigrams classifier and reported baselines' performance (e.g., Bag-of-Words, Bag-of-Bigrams, Sentence Embedding scores) alongside human and random baselines.
